The shared rustls TLS builder configures both raw TTLV/TLS and HTTPS adapters for TLS 1.3. The linked raw-TLS integrity test establishes a TLS 1.3 mutual-authenticated session and sends the request before intentionally corrupting response data; the linked HTTPS adapter test completes a TLS 1.3 exchange. These transport tests are implementation evidence only: the profile rule checks configured transport policy and does not claim live negotiation, certificate validation, peer identity, or server acceptance. The source keyword remains SHOULD; no requirement-specific official Test Case ID or profile-conformance claim is made.

requirements.subject: Result Message use
requirements.summary: When a response contains Result Message, a client may expose its exact text to the application for optional end-user display or caller-controlled logging or auditing.
requirements.condition: The server returns the optional Result Message in its response.
requirements.review_note: The uppercase MAY and server-to-client message direction are direct source text; assigning the separate second MAY to the consuming client application is the project interpretation in KMIPKIT-DEC-016. ResultMessage::as_str and KmipOperationResult::message expose the exact returned text to the caller. Tests verify message preservation, optional typed capability coverage, and redacted Debug output. The caller chooses whether to display, log, or audit it; KMIPKit does not automatically log Result Message content. No requirement-specific official Test Case ID is linked in the pinned OASIS Test Cases v2.1 source; no formal profile-conformance claim is made.

discrepancies.summary: Batch Error Continuation wording
alternatives: Continue means later batch items proceed without rollback, as its first description states.
Continue also undoes completed items and returns Undone statuses, as the following description states.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Batch ordering, rollback expectations, result status handling, and client-side interpretation.

alternatives: The body uses the selected TTLV, XML, or JSON encoding indicated by Content-Type.
The body is binary TTLV regardless of the listed XML and JSON Content-Type cases.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: HTTPS request and response codecs, Content-Type selection, and the TTLV-only 1.0 boundary.

discrepancies.summary: Baseline conformance points to a second mandatory test suite

discrepancies.summary: PKCS#11 Client MAY clause points to JSON Client
alternatives: The conflict boundary refers to PKCS#11 Client §5.18.3.
The printed JSON Client §5.5.2 reference is intentional.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Scope of optional additions permitted by the PKCS#11 Client profile.

discrepancies.summary: PKCS#11 Server MAY clause points to JSON Server
alternatives: The conflict boundary refers to PKCS#11 Server §5.18.4.

The reference should identify Intermediate Client conditions §5.7.2.

discrepancies.summary: Profiles §6.14 literally includes Basic Symmetric Key Foundry Client conditions; authorial intent is not textually determinable.
alternatives: Advanced Client is intentionally based on Basic Client conditions §5.7.1.

alternatives: MAY NOT is intended as a prohibition.
MAY NOT is intended as permission with a negated condition or another noncanonical meaning.

discrepancies.downstream_impact: For KMIPKit 1.0, the lowercase PKCS#12 output paragraph is descriptive server guidance, not an added RFC 2119 client obligation. The client preserves explicit request options and opaque server output without container validation.

discrepancies.summary: Lowercase may appears in a mixed client-rule block

alternatives: Use TC-SETTATTR labels from the section headings.

discrepancies.summary: Reserved-tag receipt and lossless preservation behavior is not specified
alternatives: Retain an inbound reserved tag as opaque data while preventing it from being emitted as a supported tag.
Reject an inbound reserved tag before generic preservation.

discrepancies.summary: JSON profile example uses Template for a reserved Object Type value
alternatives: Follow Specification §11.34 and keep Object Type value 0x00000006 reserved; the JSON example is erroneous.
Treat the JSON example's Template label as intended for value 0x00000006; this conflicts with the reserved registry entry.

discrepancies.summary: Query Asynchronous Requests response table is labeled as a PKCS#11 response
alternatives: Table 286 is the Query Asynchronous Requests response payload and its printed PKCS#11 caption is erroneous.
The PKCS#11 caption is intentional and the table is misplaced in the Query Asynchronous Requests operation section.

discrepancies.summary: Table 315 RNG Retrieve Errors caption is stranded in Re-Provision error handling
alternatives: Table 315 is a stray or erroneous caption in Re-Provision error handling; the RNG Retrieve Errors table is Table 318 under §6.1.49.
Table 315 is an intentionally misplaced RNG Retrieve error table, with its contents or intended role omitted from the source location.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The Table 315 caption remains an OASIS source defect pending authoritative correction. KMIPKit follows DEC-008 as a project interpretation for 1.0: treat it as stray Re-Provision material and use Table 318 for RNG Retrieve, without claiming an OASIS erratum.

discrepancies.summary: The lowercase “must” in section 9.4 has unresolved RFC 2119 classification under the uppercase key-word definition in section 1.2.
alternatives: Treat lowercase must as a case-insensitive candidate for RFC 2119 MUST classification.
Treat only uppercase RFC 2119 key words as normative and do not classify lowercase must as RFC 2119 MUST.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The RFC 2119 classification for satisfying multiple Credential structures remains unresolved; keep the affected requirement and Credential element gated.

discrepancies.summary: The section 9.11 requirement to provide at least one Device Credential field does not specify its field set.
alternatives: Interpret at least one field as any of all six Table 412 members, including Device Identifier and Password.

Interpret at least one field as at least one of the four identifier members named in the preceding uniqueness sentence: Device Serial Number, Network Identifier, Machine Identifier, or Media Identifier.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The minimum field set for a Device Credential remains unresolved; do not select or enforce either interpretation.

discrepancies.summary: Batch Error Continuation outbound value range
alternatives: Apply §9.6's SHALL literally and permit only the three assigned values Undo, Stop, and Continue in outbound requests.
Treat Table 435's Extensions allocation as permitting additional outbound values despite §9.6's three-value SHALL.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The 1.0 client needs a defined outbound value policy; generic decoding continues to preserve all raw Enumeration values. The project decision selects assigned-only emission without asserting that OASIS invalidates its extension allocation.

discrepancies.summary: Locate server obligations attributed to the client actor
alternatives: Keep the linked rows as client-facing constraints and define client evidence that can prove them without implementing a server.
Split client request/preservation duties from server ID Placeholder, group matching, and Storage Status response duties, then assign each row to its actual actor.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Five Locate rows are server-only; the Group Member Default extraction is retired because it has no independent normative keyword. Client forwarding and result preservation remain required by the 017 feature specification.

discrepancies.summary: Single-request cryptographic Data optionality when both Init and Final Indicator are true
alternatives: Apply Tables 196, 214, 235, 259, and 334: single-part requests require Data, except Sign may use Digested Data, even when both indicators are true.

Apply §6.1 paragraph 009 literally: Data may be omitted when either indicator is true, including the framed single-request form with both indicators true and no Correlation Value; for Sign, the independent Digested Data alternative remains subject to Table 334.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: KMIPKIT-DEC-015 records the project reading: operation tables govern single-part Data requiredness, including framed true/true single-part requests; Sign retains its Digested Data alternative. For multi-part requests, table Data=No is not universal permission or universal requiredness: paragraph 009 requires Data when neither indicator is true and permits omission when either is true. No paragraph-009 requirement ID or external conformance claim is created.

discrepancies.summary: Streaming test case descriptions and linked XML disagree on Decrypt items
alternatives: The §2.100 HTML description names Encrypt and Decrypt, but its linked XML contains no Decrypt item; the §2.101 HTML description names Encrypt only.
The linked §2.101 XML contains four Decrypt request/response pairs despite its HTML description.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Catalog operation-to-case associations follow the HTML descriptions, while fixture-derived tests use only operation items present in XML. The actual Decrypt pairs in KMIPKIT-0019 come from §2.101, not §2.100; do not synthesize missing items or claim a complete case pass.

discrepancies.summary: Query empty-response prose conflicts with required Protection Storage Masks field
alternatives: Apply the §6.1.40 prose: when there are no values to return, the response payload is empty and the Table 283 Protection Storage Masks field is absent.
Apply Table 283: a structured successful response includes the required Protection Storage Masks field; when the server cannot or will not provide values, its list is empty.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Query response decoding and any assessment of server conformance for empty or unavailable Query results.

discrepancies.summary: Verification response tables omit the final multi-part Validity Indicator required by operation prose
alternatives: Apply Tables 263 and 338 literally: Validity Indicator is present for a single-part response and absent for all multi-part responses.
Apply the prose in §§6.1.33 and 6.1.56: Validity Indicator is present for a single-part or final multi-part response and absent for non-final multi-part responses.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Typed MAC Verify and Signature Verify response cardinality for the final multi-part response and any assessment of server conformance for that case.

discrepancies.summary: Table 364 uses sentence-case “May be repeated” for Derivation Data
alternatives: Treat sentence-case May as a normative MAY that creates an independent client capability obligation.
Treat only uppercase keyword usage as carrying defined special meaning; preserve repeated fields in the schema without a separate normative requirement.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Whether repeated Derivation Data is counted as a client conformance obligation.

discrepancies.summary: Certify prose and Table 179 conflict on omitted Unique Identifier
alternatives: Follow §6.1.6 prose and require the public key's explicit Unique Identifier when Certificate Request is omitted.
Follow Table 179 and permit omission of Unique Identifier with server-side ID Placeholder substitution when Certificate Request is omitted.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Certify request validation and whether an omitted public-key identifier can consume a prior ID Placeholder.

discrepancies.summary: Re-Provision prose server obligation conflicts with optional Table 314 response identifier
alternatives: Treat the §6.1.48 prose SHALL for CSR/certificate requests as a client parsing requirement and reject successful responses that omit Unique Identifier for those request forms.
Follow Table 314 for client parsing and permit the response Unique Identifier to be absent for all three request forms, while retaining the prose SHALL as a server-side obligation where it applies.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Whether KMIPKit rejects a successful Re-Provision response without Unique Identifier; this does not change the server-side output obligation stated in the §6.1.48 prose.

discrepancies.summary: Set Endpoint Role's successful role switch is unresolved against the client-only 1.0 boundary
alternatives: Treat the §6.1.54 role-switch prose as requiring a 1.0 client to act as the server for later messages on the established channel, extending beyond the approved client-initiated-only boundary.
Limit 1.0 support to the client-initiated Set Endpoint Role exchange and defer behavior after the role switch until a scope decision is approved.
Defer the §6.1.54 operation from 1.0 until the effect of its successful role switch is resolved.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The resolution determines whether a KMIPKit client may communicate after the endpoint roles switch and whether Set Endpoint Role can be claimed in a 1.0 client profile.

discrepancies.summary: Section 9.17 contains two MAY atoms whose response-field and client-use scopes must remain distinct
alternatives: Assign the response-field MAY to the server response and the separate end-user or logging/auditing MAY to the consuming client application under KMIPKIT-DEC-016.
Assign the entire paragraph to a single server-to-client actor and direction.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: The two MAY atoms remain distinct. The first is an actor-unspecified server-to-client response-field capability. Under KMIPKIT-DEC-016, the second is represented as client-accessible use through the consuming application; KMIPKit leaves display, logging, and auditing choices to the caller and performs no automatic logging.

decisions.interpretation: KMIPKit policy decision: accept ADR-0011 for KMIPKit 1.0 and reject a received TTLV Tag classified as Reserved by ADR-0010 before constructing the public generic Item tree. Unknown Tags in the accepted 0x54 extension range remain eligible for decoding. OASIS KMIP Specification v2.1 §11.56 identifies the standard and extension Tag ranges but does not prescribe this receiver policy.
decisions.approval_evidence: Direct maintainer instruction on 2026-10-05 authorized autonomous execution of the KMIPKIT-0005 plan without further approval or manual intervention. The selected project policy and delegated approval are documented in docs/adr/0011-reserved-tag-decoding-policy.md and specs/005-ttlv-wire-codec/approval-record.md.
decisions.consequence: Reserved Tags received from the wire fail decoding before generic Item construction; the OASIS registry classification and ADR-0010 precedence rule remain unchanged.

decisions.interpretation: KMIPKit 1.0 outbound policy for the initial typed client accepts only the assigned Batch Error Continuation values Undo, Stop, and Continue. Generic decoding preserves every raw Enumeration value. This conservative project behavior follows §9.6's literal three-value SHALL while preserving Table 435's Extensions allocation in the catalog; it does not assert that OASIS makes extension-range values invalid. The separate KMIPKIT-DISC-001 concerning Continue/Undo execution effects remains open and is not affected.
decisions.approval_evidence: The maintainer directly authorized autonomous execution of the complete KMIPKit plan without further approval requests or manual intervention. This specific disposition and its limits are recorded in docs/adr/0013-client-extension-registry-ownership.md and specs/007-client-execution/approval-record.md.
decisions.consequence: The initial client sends assigned values only; vendor extension-range values remain preservable as raw data but are not emitted by KMIPKIT-0007. A later registered extension feature or an authoritative OASIS clarification may propose a reviewed policy change. No Continue/Undo execution or rollback behavior is inferred.

The uppercase key-format requirements elsewhere in the section remain in force. The client preserves the requested format and returned KMIP object without constructing, decrypting, or validating a PKCS#12 container.

decisions.interpretation: Table 464 in §11.28 states there SHALL be only one replacement object per Managed Object but does not name the actor. For the 1.0 client scope, interpret this as a server-side managed-object invariant: operation-specific §§6.1.45–6.1.47 explicitly require the server to create replacement links. KMIPKit adds no local preflight validation duty. The source uses “Replacement Key”/“Replaced Key” in §6.1.47 while §11.28/Table 465 names “Replacement Object Link”/“Replaced Object Link”; preserve and document this source terminology discrepancy without editing upstream.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct clarification in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: On 2026-10-10 the maintainer explicitly approved the server-side reading, no client prevalidation, and documentation of the §6.1.47 naming difference for KMIPKIT-DISC-023.
decisions.consequence: Client conformance does not require local detection/rejection of a second replacement. The server must create links according to the operation sections. Public models retain wire Link values losslessly and the source naming difference remains visible.

decisions.interpretation: Apply OASIS KMIP Specification v2.1 §1.2: the defined RFC 2119 keywords are uppercase, as clarified by RFC 8174. The lowercase optional and may in the HKDF paragraph of §7.12 and the sentence-case “May be repeated” in Table 364 are descriptive and create no independent normative client obligation. Preserve the described Hashing Algorithm override in Cryptographic Parameters, which Table 364 lists as a field, without requiring a non-default hash. Preserve repeated Derivation Data occurrences as represented by Table 364, without counting that sentence-case wording as a normative MAY. The distinct uppercase MAY and SHALL in §7.12 remain normative: the client can select explicit Derivation Data or a Secret Data object Unique Identifier; if both are supplied, the server SHALL return an error.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct clarification in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: On 2026-10-10 the maintainer directed that the OASIS KMIP definition control and that the recommended interpretation be used where OASIS has no applicable rule.
decisions.consequence: The client represents the Hashing Algorithm override and repeated Derivation Data without claiming independent normative duties to use a non-default hash or repeated values. Both derivation input sources remain representable; KMIPKit does not pre-reject a request containing both and surfaces the server error required by §7.12.

decisions.interpretation: Follow the §6.1.6 prose: if Certificate Request is omitted, the client explicitly supplies the public key's Unique Identifier. Do not apply the conflicting Table 179 sentence as an ID Placeholder substitution for this request input. Unique Identifier may still be omitted when Certificate Request Value is present. The generated certificate's returned identifier may still be consumed by a subsequent Get in the same ordered batch through the ID Placeholder mechanism.

decisions.consequence: The client rejects Certify requests that omit both Certificate Request Value and Unique Identifier; it preserves omission of Unique Identifier when request material is present and retains the output ID Placeholder path for a following Get. Pinned OASIS source files remain unchanged.

decisions.interpretation: Follow Table 314 for the KMIPKit client response parser: Unique Identifier remains optional and may be absent from a successful Re-Provision response for any of the three supported request forms. Preserve a returned identifier and do not synthesize one. The §6.1.48 prose SHALL to return an identifier for CSR and certificate forms remains a server-side obligation; the parameterless lowercase “shall” is not an uppercase normative keyword under §1.2.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct clarification in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: On 2026-10-11 the maintainer selected the Table 314 interpretation, keeping Unique Identifier optional in parsed Re-Provision responses, including CSR and certificate forms.
decisions.consequence: The current Re-Provision parser contract and optional-identifier tests remain unchanged. The specification and catalog now record the prose/table discrepancy and distinguish client parsing from the server-side SHALL. Pinned OASIS source files remain unchanged.

decisions.interpretation: For single-part requests, Tables 196, 214, 235, 259, and 334 control Data requiredness even when Init Indicator and Final Indicator are both true and Correlation Value is absent; Table 334 keeps Digested Data as the Sign alternative to Data. For multi-part requests, a table value of No does not make Data universally required: §6.1 paragraph 009 requires Data when both indicators are absent or false, and omission is permitted when either indicator is true. This is our recommended reading of the source tension and preserves the distinction between single-part and multi-part shapes. The paragraph uses lowercase “required”, not the formal RFC keyword REQUIRED. No standalone paragraph-009 requirement ID or formal conformance claim is created.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct authorization in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: The user directed this task to treat pinned OASIS KMIP 2.1 as the source of truth and use best judgment where it does not uniquely decide.
decisions.consequence: Existing request validation remains unchanged: Encrypt, Decrypt, Hash, and MAC require Data for single-part requests, including the framed true/true form; Sign permits Digested Data as its single-part alternative. In multi-part requests, Data is required when neither indicator is true and may be omitted when either is true. The operation-table rows and paragraph-009 clause receive no standalone REQ ID; the pinned OASIS source files remain immutable.

decisions.interpretation: Keep the first §9.17 MAY as an optional server-to-client response-field capability; the source does not name its actor. For the separate MAY to provide the returned text to an end user or use it for logging/auditing, assign the consuming client application as the actor because KMIPKit exposes the response value to its caller. This is a project interpretation of an unnamed endpoint. The client may inspect the exact text and decide whether to display, log, or audit it; KMIPKit does not automatically log Result Message content.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct authorization in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: The user directed this task to treat pinned OASIS KMIP 2.1 as the source of truth and use best judgment where it does not uniquely decide.
decisions.consequence: The oracle keeps the two MAY atoms separate: the first remains actor-unspecified/server-only and the second is client/client_1_0. The client requirement links to the existing ResultMessage and KmipOperationResult accessors, whose tests verify preserved text and redacted Debug output. End-user display and logging remain caller-controlled; no logging behavior is added and no formal profile-conformance claim is made.

decisions.interpretation: Profiles v2.1 §6.13 item 3 and §6.14 item 3 say SHALL support Basic Symmetric Key Foundry Client conditions in §5.7.1. These literal §5.7.1 references are normative and control the profile closures. Keep both normative-inclusion edges to §5.7.1 and preserve those inherited requirements in the Intermediate and Advanced profile closures. The section titles and separate test-case requirements in §5.7.2, §5.7.6, §5.7.3, and §5.7.7 may indicate possible authorial intent to reference profile-specific conditions, but that intent is not established by the normative text and does not change the normative inclusion. Record that possible intent as explanatory context only; do not correct or modify the pinned OASIS source and do not create standalone requirement IDs.

decisions.approval_evidence: The user directed this task to use pinned KMIP 2.1 as the source of truth and apply the best-supported interpretation where the text does not uniquely decide.
decisions.consequence: DISC-011 and DISC-012 no longer block source applicability closure. The catalog and independent oracle retain the literal inclusions to §5.7.1; possible authorial intent remains documented without altering the source or profile requirement arrays.

decisions.interpretation: For KMIP Specification v2.1 §§10.1.2, 10.1.5, and 11.56, retain the source actor and direction as unspecified: the clauses specify TTLV encoding and tag rules without naming an endpoint. Map the existing mandatory IDs to client-to-server encoding for KMIPKit 1.0 profiles that use TTLV: the 14 client_1_0 profiles and the conditional HTTPS Client. The JSON, XML, and PKCS#11 profile records remain outside KMIPKit 1.0 scope. For Profiles v2.1 §4.1.2, retain the source actor and direction as unresolved because the SHALL names a Profile-conformant implementation and combines test-procedure variations with client behavior. Map its existing requirement as a shared evidence/conformance gate for a claim to any of the 18 client profiles; it is not unconditional production runtime behavior.
decisions.approver: KMIPKit maintainer, direct authorization in current task
decisions.approval_evidence: The user directed pinned OASIS KMIP 2.1 to be authoritative and authorized the best-supported project interpretation wherever the normative text is silent.
decisions.consequence: The source oracle and catalog crosswalk retain exact OASIS actor/direction facts separately from the client interpretation. Six existing TTLV requirements map to the 15 in-scope TTLV client profiles. The existing Profiles §4.1.2 SHALL maps to all 18 client profile records as a conditional conformance-evidence gate. No new normative IDs, runtime rule, OASIS source edit, profile-readiness claim, or conformance claim is added.
